reason: The hypothesis proposes a single, overarching mechanism—short-range chemical order (SRO) governed by an optimal Al content—to simultaneously explain phase stability and a broad suite of properties (high-temperature strength, environmental resistance, radiation tolerance, cryogenic toughness). No single passage links SRO to all these properties, nor does any passage propose an 'optimal' Al content for maximizing SRO to stabilize a single-phase matrix and lock in this specific combination of performance attributes. The idea synthesizes disparate observations (clustering/ordering, irradiation resistance, phase stability) into a unified, testable framework that is not stated in the literature.
copied_elements: Al content influences phase stability (P6, P20, P40)
SRO exists in Al-Cr-Co-Fe-Ni (P1, P4, P5)
SRO can be measured by diffuse scattering (P1, P4)
High configurational entropy stabilizes single-phase (P2, P10)
